Ethmoid Bone|.text: Within the nasal cavity, the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone forms the upper portion of the nasal septum.
Ethmoid Bone|.label: 7.2 Ethmoid Bone

Ethmoid Bone|.text: The ethmoid bone also forms the lateral walls of the upper nasal cavity.
Ethmoid Bone|.label: 7.2 Ethmoid Bone

Frontal Bone|.text: The frontal bone is the single bone that forms the forehead.
Frontal Bone|.label: 7.2 Frontal Bone

Frontal Bone|.text: The frontal bone also forms the supraorbital margin of the orbit.
Frontal Bone|.label: 7.2 Frontal Bone

Parietal Bone|.text: These are paired bones, with the right and left parietal bones joining together at the top of the skull.
Parietal Bone|.label: 7.2 Parietal Bone

Parietal Bone|.text: Each parietal bone is also bounded anteriorly by the frontal bone, inferiorly by the temporal bone, and posteriorly by the occipital bone.
Parietal Bone|.label: 7.2 Parietal Bone

Temporal Bone|.text: Common wisdom has it that the temporal bone (temporal = “time”) is so named because this area of the head (the temple) is where hair typically first turns gray, indicating the passage of time.
Temporal Bone|.label: 7.2 Temporal Bone

Temporal Bone|.text: The flattened, upper portion is the squamous portion of the temporal bone.
Temporal Bone|.label: 7.2 Temporal Bone

Occipital Bone|.text: On its outside surface, at the posterior midline, is a small protrusion called the external occipital protuberance, which serves as an attachment site for a ligament of the posterior neck.
Occipital Bone|.label: 7.2 Occipital Bone

Occipital Bone|.text: Lateral to either side of this bump is a superior nuchal line (nuchal = “nape” or “posterior neck”).
Occipital Bone|.label: 7.2 Occipital Bone

Sphenoid Bone|.text: It serves as a “keystone” bone, because it joins with almost every other bone of the skull.
Sphenoid Bone|.label: 7.2 Sphenoid Bone

Sphenoid Bone|.text: Inside the cranial cavity, the right and left lesser wings of the sphenoid bone, which resemble the wings of a flying bird, form the lip of a prominent ridge that marks the boundary between the anterior and middle cranial fossae.
Sphenoid Bone|.label: 7.2 Sphenoid Bone

Inferior Nasal Conchae|.text: The inferior concha is the largest of the nasal conchae and can easily be seen when looking into the anterior opening of the nasal cavity.
Inferior Nasal Conchae|.label: 7.2 Inferior Nasal Conchae

Lacrimal Bone|.text: The anterior portion of the lacrimal bone forms a shallow depression called the lacrimal fossa, and extending inferiorly from this is the nasolacrimal canal.
Lacrimal Bone|.label: 7.2 Lacrimal Bone

Lacrimal Bone|.text: The lacrimal fluid (tears of the eye), which serves to maintain the moist surface of the eye, drains at the medial corner of the eye into the nasolacrimal canal.
Lacrimal Bone|.label: 7.2 Lacrimal Bone

Maxillary Bone|.text: Each tooth is anchored into a deep socket called an alveolus.
Maxillary Bone|.label: 7.2 Maxillary Bone

Maxillary Bone|.text: On the anterior maxilla, just below the orbit, is the infraorbital foramen.
Maxillary Bone|.label: 7.2 Maxillary Bone

Nasal Bone|.text: The nasal bone is one of two small bones that articulate (join) with each other to form the bony base (bridge) of the nose.
Nasal Bone|.label: 7.2 Nasal Bone

Nasal Bone|.text: These are the bones that are damaged when the nose is broken.
Nasal Bone|.label: 7.2 Nasal Bone

Palatine Bone|.text: The palatine bone is one of a pair of irregularly shaped bones that contribute small areas to the lateral walls of the nasal cavity and the medial wall of each orbit.
Palatine Bone|.label: 7.2 Palatine Bone

Palatine Bone|.text: The largest region of each of the palatine bone is the horizontal plate.
Palatine Bone|.label: 7.2 Palatine Bone

Zygomatic Bone|.text: The zygomatic bone is also known as the cheekbone.
Zygomatic Bone|.label: 7.2 Zygomatic Bone

Mandible|.text: The mandible forms the lower jaw and is the only moveable bone of the skull.
Mandible|.label: 7.2 Mandible

Mandible|.text: At the time of birth, the mandible consists of paired right and left bones, but these fuse together during the first year to form the single U-shaped mandible of the adult skull.
Mandible|.label: 7.2 Mandible

Vomer Bone|.text: In this view, the vomer is seen to form the entire height of the nasal septum.
Vomer Bone|.label: 7.2 Vomer Bone

Vomer Bone|.text: A much smaller portion of the vomer can also be seen when looking into the anterior opening of the nasal cavity.
Vomer Bone|.label: 7.2 Vomer Bone

Hyoid Bone|.text: It is a small U-shaped bone located in the upper neck near the level of the inferior mandible, with the tips of the “U” pointing posteriorly.
Hyoid Bone|.label: 7.2 Hyoid Bone

Hyoid Bone|.text: The hyoid serves as the base for the tongue above, and is attached to the larynx below and the pharynx posteriorly.
Hyoid Bone|.label: 7.2 Hyoid Bone
